title: Path Tracing Optimizations in Indiana Jones: Opacity MicroMaps and Compaction of Dynamic BLASs
author: Louis Bavoil
summary: The article describes release2024 Indiana Jones optimizations. Unknown OMM states retain alpha checks; indirect rays may use an approximate two-state option. Dynamic vegetation BLAS compaction permits updates/refits, but subsequent rebuilds need different handling. Its Peru measurements used RTX5080, 4K output with DLSS-RR Performance/1080p tracing, High/FullRT/AllLights/Ultra vegetation and prior SER changes. TraceMain7.90→3.58ms is pass-specific; BLAS1027→606MB is not total VRAM. The documented engine is Forward+; this cannot be inferred from screenshots.
processTeachingCandidates: Opaque/transparent/unknown microtriangle decision and the retained alpha-test fallback.
Build/compact/update/refit versus rebuild; distinguish geometry memory from entire application VRAM.
Read original runtime/debug conditions before a pass-time comparison.

additionalPrimarySource.summary: SER regroups RayGen work after tracing; live variables stored across calls can increase memory traffic. In the documented shipping implementation, a one-path loop could become a branch, avoiding72 spilled bytes. Selected precision changes and dependency reduction were specific verified optimizations. On RTX5080 Peru/4K output/DLSS-RR Performance/High/FullRT/AllLights/Ultra vegetation, the comparison with SER kept ON reduced TraceMain3.63→3.08ms and spilled state222→84bytes. A separate after-optimization SER OFF/ON comparison was4.07→3.08ms. Neither is a universal full-frame speedup. Versions compared retained other optimizations, and the shipping changes date to December2024.
